title: Establish rolling clearance channel and triage playbook for PRD scope deviations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Problem: PRD scope changes and last-minute requirement clarifications frequently cause delays in signoff; reviews stall when engineering, design, or legal need fast alignment. Goal: Create a lightweight, rolling clearance channel + triage playbook to accelerate cross-team acceptance for PRD changes that impact runtime, data residency, or customer SLAs. This ticket captures scope, acceptance criteria, and first-run runbook for a pilot with Runtime, Design, and Legal reps. The playbook should be skimmable (<2 pages), include a timeline for response SLAs, explicit decision owners for common risk classes, and a standardized artifact checklist (PRD diff, security/data flow, UX impact, rollout rollback plan).
acceptance_criteria: A concise rolling clearance channel (Slack/Spaces + dedicated triage thread) is created and documented
A two-page triage playbook exists covering: risk classes, response SLAs, artifact checklist, and decision owners
Pilot run completed on at least two PRD scope changes and each case has end-to-end timestamps showing reduced signoff latency by >=40%
Design, Engineering, and Legal representatives sign off on the playbook and agree to the SLAs
Playbook includes explicit fallback path (who can greenlight temporary scope freeze) and rollback criteria
success_metrics: Median PRD signoff time for scope changes falls below 72 hours during pilot
>80% of triage items resolved within initial SLA window (24 hours for urgent, 72 for standard)
Fewer postponed launches attributed to signoff blockers (target: 50% reduction)
